result_text:
The four broken default conventions now match what they were meant to. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (335 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped), and I did not commit.

Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **HTML pages:** the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules now use `(htm|html|xhtml)` instead of `(html|html|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages are covered.
- **.NET docs and JavaScript:** `.*/[.]xml` and `.*/[.]js` became `.*[.]xml` and `.*[.]js`. The old patterns required a `/` before the dot, so they only matched a bare `.xml` or `.js`.
- **Gradle JavaScript:** `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` became `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

I also added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks that the affected files land in the right scope and that hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files stay out, along with the existing matches (`build.gradle`, Doxygen `.html`, `.xhtml` with a generator meta tag). It passes 5/5.

One thing I did not change: the meta-generator content pattern is `[ ]*[<]meta name[=]"generator" .*`. Content patterns are matched per full line, so this only fires when the `<meta>` tag starts its line. A tag preceded by other markup on the same line would be missed. That's outside the four typos you listed, so I left it alone.
